claims.text: Mechanical alloying or powder handling can introduce oxygen into Ti-containing refractory HEA powders, potentially reaching about 0.8 wt%.
Thermal decomposition of TiH2 or ZrH2 under ultra-high vacuum removes hydrogen from the precursor powder.
Maintaining pressure below 10^-6 Pa during hydride decomposition prevents consequential oxygen ingress.
Vacuum hydride decomposition can keep or reduce bulk oxygen below 0.8 wt% even when the starting powder is near or above that concentration.
In HfNbTaTiZr, an oxygen concentration near 0.8 wt% marks the onset of strong oxygen-associated hardening.
High oxygen concentrations in HfNbTaTiZr are associated with embrittlement and cracking during deformation.
The approximately 0.8 wt% oxygen threshold measured for HfNbTaTiZr is applicable as a critical embrittlement limit for other Group-IV-containing refractory HEAs.
Heating faster than 100 °C/min to 1200 °C suppresses nucleation of brittle alpha-HCP phases.
Ostwald's Rule implies that rapid heating, rather than cooling or crystallization, prevents the thermodynamic drive toward alpha-HCP formation in Group-IV refractory HEAs.
Residual oxygen in a Ti-containing refractory HEA can form TiO precipitates because Ti has high oxygen affinity.
Fine TiO particles in a BCC refractory HEA matrix impede dislocation motion and increase strength.
The TiO precipitates produced by the proposed process will be coherent with the BCC matrix.
TiO precipitates stabilize the metastable BCC solid solution.
The absence of alpha-HCP phases prevents grain-boundary embrittlement.
Hot swaging HfNbTaTiZr at 950 °C can produce severe cracking and inhomogeneous porosity.
Using a higher deformation temperature and lower strain rate than the reported 950 °C swaging process will avoid catastrophic cracking.
Rapid extrusion densification at 1200 °C will produce a crack-free bulk body with greater than 95% density.
TiO precipitation will enhance yield strength at 800-1000 °C.
Suppressing alpha-HCP and TCP phases will preserve ductility above room temperature.
Conventional extrusion or swaging of Group-IV refractory HEAs typically causes oxygen uptake above 0.8 wt%, alpha-HCP formation, and catastrophic cracking.

contradictions.description: The starting powder may already contain at least 0.8 wt% oxygen, but the proposed intervention only removes hydrogen and prevents additional oxygen ingress. No oxygen-removal step is specified, so the claim that the process keeps bulk oxygen below 0.8 wt% does not follow for an initially over-threshold powder.

The structural mediator and strength prediction require TiO precipitates, while the predicted outcome also permits a single-phase BCC product. A genuinely single-phase BCC product cannot obtain its stated strength from TiO precipitation.
